signals.title: USD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Rate Divergence
signals.text: The G10 scorecard confirms USD as the dominant leader (+1.448% across 9 pairs) against JPY as the persistent laggard (−1.119% across 7 pairs), producing an extreme bilateral spread of 2.567%. USD/JPY trades at 157.88, breaking above its SMA20 (156.89) following the Bank of Japan's rate hike to 1.25%, which markets absorbed as an overtly dovish step that failed to alter wider policy divergence. The policy spread between the Fed's 4.0% hiking stance and the BoJ's 1.2% policy rate maintains a +280bp carry cushion (+264bp on OIS SOFR vs TONA), anchoring institutional dollar demand. VIX at 15.3 indicates a normal volatility regime, precluding broad flight-to-safety flows from cushioning JPY depreciation. USD/JPY 25d risk reversals sit at an extreme −2.08 put skew alongside a negative vol risk premium of −1.2% (IV 9.2% vs HV30 10.4%), highlighting heavy downside option hedging against an otherwise unhedged spot advance. Key technical resistance sits at the SMA200 (158.40) and SMA50 (159.14), with 160.00 serving as the historical trigger level for official currency intervention. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; wide rate differential favors continued top-end pressure while volatility stays anchored. Catalyst: US Industrial Production release today at 13:15 UTC. Risk: Spot rejection and close below the SMA20 at 156.89 accompanied by verbal warnings from the Ministry of Finance.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long Positioning + Policy Divergence
signals.text: CFTC positioning data reveals leveraged funds hold an extended net long of +48,379 contracts in AUD, placing positioning in the 93rd percentile of its 52-week historical distribution with a z-score of +1.72. RBA holds at 4.35%. AUD/USD trades at 0.7125, holding between its rising SMA50 (0.7084) and capping SMA20 (0.7170). The cash rate differential provides underlying support, with RBA at 4.35% vs Fed at 4.0% maintaining a −35bp carry advantage in favor of AUD (−73bp on AONIA vs SOFR basis). However, a 25d risk reversal skew of −0.71 demonstrates that options markets are pricing downside protection, signaling reluctance to chase spot higher into crowded positioning. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD; heavy speculative length limits sustained upside extension. Catalyst: Fed Governor Bowman speech at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Leveraged funds net positioning liquidates below +35,000 contracts, triggering an unwinding move toward the SMA200 at 0.7013.
evidence: RBA 4.35% vs Fed 4.0% — -35bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: GBP/USD — Policy Hold + Technical Compression
signals.text: The BoE holds at 3.75%. Spot GBP/USD trades at 1.3344, printing below its entire moving average complex with the SMA200 (1.3455), SMA50 (1.3482), and SMA20 (1.3532) stacked overhead as rigid technical resistance. COT positioning shows leveraged funds long +40,361 contracts (86th percentile, z +1.02), but institutional capital is actively paring exposure with a weekly outflow of −7,143 contracts. Despite a UK retail sales beat of 2.4% y/y vs 1.5% forecast, price action remains heavy below 1.3360. Options skew remains tilted toward base weakness, with 1M 25d risk reversals registering −0.40. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; moving-average cluster overhead and steady speculative long unwinds enforce downside bias. Catalyst: US CB Leading Economic Index at 14:00 UTC. Risk: A daily close back above the SMA200 at 1.3455, invalidating the bearish technical structure.
evidence: BoE 3.75% vs Fed 4.0% — +25bp USD carry advantage

signals.title: USD/CAD — Bullish Moving Average Alignment + Carry Premium
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4013, maintaining a clean technical posture above its SMA20 (1.3858), SMA50 (1.3947), and SMA200 (1.3832). The monetary policy backdrop solidly underpins USD demand, with the Fed at 4.0% against the Bank of Canada at 2.25%, generating a wide +175bp policy spread (+133bp on SOFR vs CORRA carry basis). Leveraged funds sit heavily net short CAD at −56,852 contracts (14th percentile of 52-week range, z −1.03), though a weekly covering flow of +13,290 contracts has temporarily stabilized the base. Crude oil softness at $96.20/bbl (−1.04% intraday) limits Canadian terms-of-trade support, offsetting Canada's positive domestic Economic Surprise Index of +15.7. The 25d risk reversal remains balanced at +0.03, showing little structural options demand to fade the spot advance. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; policy spread and triple moving average alignment support higher levels. Catalyst: US Baker Hughes Oil Rig Count at 17:00 UTC. Risk: Spot break and daily close below the SMA50 support at 1.3947.
evidence: Fed 4.0% vs BoC 2.25% — +175bp USD carry premium
